one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban identifies the gut legal issue and gut policy issue in the Corona impeachment trial. Senate President Pro Tem Jinggoy Estrada nearly fell asleep during the defense's first witness Rep. Toby Tiangco -- whose testimony senators Sotto, Pangilinan, Lacson, and Angara deemed 'irrelevant' -- because what was expected was an explanation of the SALN omissions and undervaluations. Senate President Enrile told the defense: 'They should go directly to the substance of Article 2.' The gut legal issue is whether the assets Corona failed to disclose are manifestly out of proportion to his lawful income -- triggering dismissal under RA 3019 and prima facie unlawfully acquired status under RA 1379. The Senate's March 6, 2012 resolution formally admitted the bank deposit evidence, linking it to the SALNs to compare what was declared from 2005 to 2010 against actual balances. The defense heeded senators' warnings and began presenting evidence -- CJ withholds judgment on adequacy until full ventilation. Beyond the legal issues, the gut policy issue -- Corona's fitness to remain as Chief Justice -- is actively debated outside the court. Corona went on a media blitz pledging readiness to testify, open dollar accounts, and accept the Senate's verdict, and branded the Basa revelations as lies. But simultaneously, his lawyers told Sen. Trillanes there was no necessity for Corona to testify or open accounts and filed petitions in the SC on February 8 and 13 to nullify the entire proceedings. CJ closes on the damaging dichotomy: how will the people and senator-judges view this conflict between Corona's political posture and his lawyers' legal stance?
